messages:
Alex: pushed a batch of KV-cache prefetch + throttle experiments across regions (us / eu / apac) and GPU families (H100 / A100). goal: understand hit-rate vs latency tradeoffs by seqlen mix. attaching raw numbers and short notes. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Maya: awesome — did you use the same request distribution as production?

Alex: yes, used last-30d sampled seqlen histogram (prod-mix-2026-03) + two synthetic mixes (short-heavy, long-tail). run command: 
```
./perf/run_kv_bench --model gptx-13b-q8 --regions us,eu,apac --gpus H100,A100 --slen-config prod-mix.json --prefetch 0.2 --throttle 0.6 --evict-policy lru
```

Sanjay: quick notes: prefetch=0.2 means we prefetch 20% of predicted next blocks; throttle=0.6 is our admission control for background prefetch jobs. evictions were LRU; we also tried size-aware LRU in a followup.

Ingrid: paste of high-level numbers (aggregate across 10k samples per config):
- H100/us (prod-mix): cache hit 86%, p50=6ms, p95=18ms, p99=45ms
- A100/us (prod-mix): cache hit 83%, p50=8ms, p95=24ms, p99=62ms
- H100/eu (prod-mix): cache hit 84%, p50=7ms, p95=20ms, p99=50ms
- H100/apac (prod-mix, higher paging): cache hit 78%, p50=9ms, p95=30ms, p99=110ms (spikes due to paging/evict thrash)

Maya: interesting — apac has higher p99. is that due to different slen mix or kernel selection?

Alex: dug in — apac experiments landed on a fallback kernel for long sequences because of a lower CUDA-driver version on that region's node image. that fallback increases token latency by ~2x when working off-disk pages.

Sanjay: concrete eviction behavior: when long-tail queries hit (seqlen >= 2k) we see KV page churn: eviction rate goes up ~3x and hit-rate drops ~12 percentage points. prefetch helps short-tail (slen < 256) a lot, but hurts tail because it warms pages that get evicted before reuse.

Ingrid: per-slen bucket summary (H100/us, prod-mix, prefetch=0.2/throttle=0.6):
- 1-128: hit 94%, p99 12ms
- 129-512: hit 88%, p99 28ms
- 513-2048: hit 72%, p99 85ms
- >2048: hit 41%, p99 320ms (mostly disk fetches)

Alex: we also compared eviction policies: LRU vs LRU-size-aware vs LFU. size-aware wins for long-tail mixed workloads: improves hit-rate for >512 by ~6pp and reduces p99 for >2048 by ~25%.

Maya: did you try increasing throttle (lower background prefetch) to reduce thrash?

Alex: yes. throttle=0.2 (more aggressive prefetch) -> short-tail p99 drops 15%, but long-tail p99 increases 40%. throttle=0.9 (minimal prefetch) -> long-tail p99 improves, but short-tail p50/p95 regress. tradeoff depends on SLA weightings.

Sanjay: capacity sizing note: baseline H100 pool with prefetch=0.2 sustained 1200 reqs/s at target p95=30ms for prod-mix; with throttle=0.9 we could scale down to ~1050 reqs/s while keeping p95 under 35ms. A100 needs ~1.25x capacity for same SLO.

Ingrid: action items:
1) patch region images to ensure consistent kernel selection (apac fallback is causing extra page I/O).
2) add size-aware eviction as default in Dedicated pools behind a feature flag.
3) expose throttle knob in console per-pool and add recommended presets (short-heavy, balanced, tail-optimized).

Alex: I've opened a PR with the benches + config files: https://git.redwood.ai/r/inference/kv-bench/compare/PR-452 (raw CSVs attached). ci-bot ran validations.

ci-bot: Perf job completed: all runs passed, no config errors. artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/kvcache/1847774210/*

Maya: can someone generate the per-region heatmap (hit-rate vs p99) for the README? i'll add it to the eval dashboard.

Alex: on it, exporting charts now. will drop links in this thread. :thumbsup:

Ingrid: great work. recommend we schedule a 20m sync with platform next week to decide rollouts.

Sanjay: +1, include a note about planned kernel rollouts and the capacity delta for A100.

Alex: thanks all, will follow up with artifacts and a short PR summary.
